sub_indicators.label: Citizen feedback channel
sub_indicators.subject: include.access
sub_indicators.text: Citizen feedback portals: citizen feedback channel
sub_indicators.norm_short: The AU Charter on Decentralisation asks that ICT be used so residents can give feedback to their representatives; the UN E-Participation Index ranks e-information, e-consultation and e-decision-making.
criteria: A source from the past three years says people have no digital channel to complain about or comment on public services.
A government body has launched, piloted or is preparing a web portal, app or messaging service through which people report problems with or complain about public services.
A digital complaints or feedback channel is in service and a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled is on record.
A national channel takes complaints about the services of most ministries or of local governments, or routes them to the bodies responsible across government.
The share of complaints resolved, response times, or a report of the cases and what was done about them is published.
